articles.headline: France, Argentina top World Cup odds; U.S. puts sportsbooks at risk
articles.description: Star-powered France and Argentina top the odds board to win the World Cup as the tournament moves into the knockout stage, while the United States' positive momentum will have sportsbooks sweating more with each game it

articles.headline: Why every round-of-32 team will, won't win FIFA World Cup
articles.description: Then there were 32. Or we're getting there, anyway. So, let's review why each team still alive at the 2026 World Cup could win the whole thing -- and why each probably won't.

articles.headline: Every team's championship odds for the 2026 World Cup
articles.description: Odds for every team to advance through the knockout stage and to win the 2026 World Cup.

articles.headline: Aubrey Modiba: Canada must beware of Bafana 'upset' despite 'home' advantage
articles.description: South Africa's Aubrey Modiba is quietly confident that Bafana Bafana can add to the World Cup's growing list of surprise results when they face Canada in their Last 32 match in Inglewood on Sunday.

articles.headline: Bafana's World Cup clash with Canada can change South Africa's football trajectory
articles.description: When Hugo Broos' Bafana Bafana face Canada in the FIFA World Cup round of 32 at Los Angeles Stadium, a win could make a major difference to South Africa's football ecosystem.

articles.headline: Yaya Sithole's redemption arc key to South Africa's recovery from disastrous start at FIFA World Cup
articles.description: Yaya Sithole could have been forgiven for questioning whether he was in a waking nightmare midway through his first ever FIFA World Cup game, for South Africa against Mexico on July 11.
